# Aneural — Device Litigation Intelligence Portal

> Verified litigation intelligence for the top revenue-ranked medical devices: adverse-event exhibits, paid-expert overlap, 510(k) predicate family trees, demand mapping, sponsor trial AEs, and global regulatory footprint — every figure cited to a named dataset. Pre-computed, human-verified JSON; agents should present it with its caveats, never recompose or extrapolate it.

Machine-readable manifest: https://aneural-portal.pages.dev/agent.json
Device page: https://aneural-portal.pages.dev/?d=<slug> — module anchor: #mod-<moduleId>

## Caveats — read these first (present them with the data)

- Payment records are sourced facts from CMS Open Payments (manufacturer-reported). Co-occurrence of payments and advocacy is presented for investigation; it is not an assertion that any physician was improperly influenced.
- Facility-grain CMS procedure volumes are a lawful geographic proxy for where device procedures concentrate. MAUDE carries no patient geography; no patient-level claim is made. Hospital star ratings are hospital-wide CMS quality measures, not device-specific. CMS suppresses cells under 11 discharges, so facility volumes are floors.
- Sponsor-reported adverse-event tables from the trial registry (results section), aggregated per study arm — a subject can appear under multiple terms and arms, so subject counts are not deduplicated across rows. The registry has no death event type; deaths are counted via death-worded terms. Trials matched by intervention name (device scope) or lead sponsor (manufacturer scope, labeled).
- Matched by author/party NAME (registry identity cannot be linked across these datasets); each item is graded 'corroborated' (an independent signal beyond the name matched) or 'name-only' (could be a different person with the same name). Nothing is silently excluded.
- AACT database, Clinical Trials Transformation Initiative (CTTI) — the relational parse of ClinicalTrials.gov

## Modules (per device; anchor #mod-<id>)

- narratives: MAUDE adverse-event exhibit (untangled narratives) — $2,500
- trial-aes: Sponsor trial adverse-event exhibit (registry) — $2,500
- global-actions: Global regulatory footprint (7 jurisdictions) — $2,500
- predicate-tree: 510(k) predicate family tree — $12,000
- experts: Paid-KOL overlap, ranked (device-anchored) — $2,500
- icp-map: Demand Map — targeting intelligence — $2,500/mo
- corporate: Corporate context panel (included with the dossier) — included
- ip: USPTO filings portfolio — $300
